policy.purpose: Prevent aggregate literary scores from hiding provider failures on specific novel genres, narrative forms, cast structures, and identity stressors.
policy.adoptionRule: A character-identity candidate must report every applicable stratum. Aggregate quality alone is insufficient for adoption.

litbankStrata.label: Romance / social novel
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests honorifics, family/social relations, repeated surnames and dialogue-heavy social interaction.

litbankStrata.label: Gothic / horror
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests embedded narration, supernatural vocabulary, titles, journals and ambiguous human/non-human references.

litbankStrata.label: Detective / mystery
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests aliases, withheld identity, dense dialogue, evidence-focused narration and recurring role nouns.

litbankStrata.label: Adventure
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests travel/location density, nicknames, crews/groups and first-person narration.

litbankStrata.label: Speculative / science fiction
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests unusual entity classes, invented concepts and person/non-person separation.

litbankStrata.label: Children's / youth fiction
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests nonstandard names, personified entities, child-focused dialogue and simpler but alias-rich prose.

litbankStrata.label: Historical / war fiction
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests ranks, titles, groups/factions, historical naming and military role nouns.

litbankStrata.label: Western / frontier fiction
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests nicknames, colloquial naming, sparse role mentions and action-heavy prose.

litbankStrata.label: Satire / comedy
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests exaggerated roles, ironic descriptions and frequent nominal references.

litbankStrata.label: Modernist / experimental prose
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests stream-of-consciousness, fragmented syntax, free indirect discourse and difficult mention boundaries.

litbankStrata.label: First-person narration
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests narrator self-reference and pronoun-heavy identity attachment.

litbankStrata.label: Epistolary / document-framed narration
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests letter/journal speaker shifts, addressees and repeated first/second-person pronouns.

litbankStrata.label: Multiple / nested narrators
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests narrator changes, embedded accounts and cross-section identity continuity.

litbankStrata.label: Large ensemble / social cast
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests same-surname families, many recurring minor characters and merge pressure.

litbankStrata.label: Non-human protagonist
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests personhood policy when major narrative agents are animals rather than humans.

litbankStrata.label: Archaic / eighteenth-century prose
litbankStrata.rationale: Tests older syntax, orthography, titles and discourse conventions.

litbankStrata.label: Aliases / titles / honorifics
litbankStrata.rationale: Directly stresses canonical-name admission, title stripping, aliases and reveal-aware attachment.

privateContemporaryCoverageRequirements: progression fantasy / LitRPG or web-serial style

supplementalEvaluationDatasets.licenseNote: Evaluation-only until license/usage implications are accepted; upstream repository states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the dataset reconstructs Project Gutenberg books.

supplementalEvaluationDatasets.role: supplemental fiction/fanfiction and multilingual coreference stress evaluation
supplementalEvaluationDatasets.licenseNote: CC BY-NC 4.0; evaluation-only and not a runtime dependency.

limitations: LitBank is English and mostly public-domain canonical fiction; it does not represent contemporary commercial fiction by itself.
Genre labels in this matrix are evaluation strata, not claims of exclusive literary classification; documents may appear in multiple strata.
The private contemporary suite must never commit copyrighted source text or redistribute user-owned books.
Whole-book Project Gutenberg retrieval must obey source terms and copyright law applicable to the execution jurisdiction.
